title: 3rd Truth Ease Amid Speed And Multiplicity And The Gradelessness Of Power

questions.question: What main quality of creation is emphasized at the start of the passage about plants and animals?
questions.answer: Their creation is presented as happening very quickly while still being perfectly ordered.

questions.question: Which two groups of living things are specially mentioned as examples?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: How does the passage connect ease with skill in creation?
questions.answer: It says things are brought into existence with ease, yet with great mastery, precision, and excellence.

questions.question: What difficulty does the passage say is absent even though created things are many and mixed together?
questions.answer: There is no confusion and no flaw.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can create in this way?
questions.answer: The only one who can do this is the One whose power has no limitation or hardship.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relation between great and small things for Divine power?
questions.answer: Huge and tiny things are equally easy for Divine power.

questions.question: What comparison is made between stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Creating stars is described as no harder than creating atoms.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a whole species and one individual?
questions.answer: Bringing an entire kind into existence is said to be as easy as creating one member of it.

questions.question: How does the passage compare reviving the whole earth with reviving a tree?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What example involving a tree and a seed shows the same idea?
questions.answer: Making a very large tree is said to be as easy as producing a tiny seed.

questions.question: What larger belief is supported by all these comparisons?
questions.answer: They support belief in Allah’s unique and unlimited power.

questions.question: Why does the passage end by saying these deeds happen before our eyes?
questions.answer: To show that this is not just an abstract claim but something people can observe in the world.

questions.question: What is the central claim of the passage about how living things are created?
questions.answer: Living things are created swiftly, abundantly, and with perfect order and excellence.

questions.question: Why is abundance important in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: Because producing many things without disorder points to immense power and control.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying created beings have value even though they are countless?
questions.answer: It means they are not cheap or careless products; each one still has worth and distinction.

questions.question: How does intermingling strengthen the argument in the passage?
questions.answer: Even when many things are mixed together, each is still made properly, which shows precise knowledge and power.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from speed, abundance, order, and value appearing together?
questions.answer: Such creation can come only from a single unmatched Creator.

questions.question: What does the passage say about difficulty in relation to that Creator’s power?
questions.answer: Nothing is difficult for that power.

questions.question: How is the creation of the biggest things compared with the smallest things?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy.

questions.question: What is the point of comparing a universal reality with a small individual case?
questions.answer: The point is that totality and particularity make no difference to Divine power.

questions.question: What does the example of the earth and the tree teach?
questions.answer: Reviving something vast and reviving something limited are the same in ease for Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention a seed as small as a fingernail?
questions.answer: To highlight that even the tiniest beginning is under the same effortless power as the largest forms.

questions.question: Is the passage mainly making a scientific description or a faith-based argument from observation?
questions.answer: It is making a faith-based argument using observation.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful reader understand after reading this passage?
questions.answer: A thoughtful reader should understand that the world’s ordered and skillful creation points to Allah’s unique, unlimited power.

questions.question: What verse theme introduces this section of the passage?
questions.answer: It begins with a verse about benefits taken from date palms and grapevines as a sign for people who use reason.

questions.question: In this section, what does “The Third Truth” focus on most directly?
questions.answer: It focuses on the way living things are created with speed, order, ease, skill, and value.

questions.question: Name two pairs of qualities that the passage presents together in creation.
questions.answer: Speed with order, and ease with skill.

questions.question: Why is it significant that creation is both abundant and distinguished?
questions.answer: Because having many examples usually suggests sameness or carelessness, but here each one still shows special quality.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about power if nothing is difficult for it?
questions.answer: It implies a power that is unlimited and not restricted like created beings are.

questions.question: How does the passage use comparison as a method of teaching?
questions.answer: It places large and small examples side by side to show they are equally easy for Divine power.

questions.question: What idea is taught by comparing the largest object to the smallest object?
questions.answer: Size does not create difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: What idea is taught by comparing a species to one member of that species?
questions.answer: Number does not create difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: What idea is taught by comparing the whole earth to one tree?
questions.answer: Vast scope does not create difficulty for Allah.

questions.question: What idea is taught by comparing a mountain-like tree to a tiny seed?
questions.answer: Great outward size and tiny beginnings are both under the same power.

questions.question: What role does human observation play in the final sentence?
questions.answer: It invites people to recognize these truths through things they can directly witness.

questions.question: What kind of response does the passage ask from people who think carefully?
questions.answer: It calls them to reflect and recognize the Creator’s oneness and power.

questions.question: According to the passage, what features appear together in the creation of plants and animals?
questions.answer: Rapid production, perfect order, ease, mastery, abundance, and distinction all appear together.

questions.question: Why would combining speed with careful order be meaningful in this argument?
questions.answer: Because quick action usually risks mistakes, but here speed does not lessen precision.

questions.question: Why would combining abundance with value also be meaningful?
questions.answer: Because making countless things usually lowers uniqueness, yet each created thing still has worth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about confusion and deficiency in creation?
questions.answer: It says neither confusion nor deficiency appears.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the Creator’s knowledge from this absence of confusion?
questions.answer: The Creator’s knowledge must be complete and exact.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the Creator’s power from this absence of deficiency?
questions.answer: The Creator’s power must be fully capable and unrestricted.

questions.question: How does the passage argue from visible examples to an unseen truth?
questions.answer: It uses observed patterns in creation to point to the reality of Divine power.

questions.question: What unseen truth is the passage especially trying to prove?
questions.answer: That there is one unique Creator whose power is limitless.

questions.question: Why does the passage list several comparisons instead of only one?
questions.answer: To show that the same truth holds across size, number, and scale.

questions.question: What is the effect of saying stars and atoms are alike in ease for Him?
questions.answer: It removes the idea that greater size means greater difficulty.

questions.question: What is the effect of saying the earth and a tree are alike in ease for Him?
questions.answer: It removes the idea that wider reach means greater difficulty.

questions.question: Summarize the main lesson of the whole passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The passage teaches that the ordered, skillful, and abundant creation we see points clearly to Allah’s unique and unlimited power.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the pace of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation happens with complete swiftness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the pattern or arrangement of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation is perfectly organized.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the manner in which creation happens?
questions.answer: It says creation happens with ease while still showing high skill.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the worth of created things?
questions.answer: It describes them as valuable and distinct.

questions.question: What challenge is mentioned alongside abundance?
questions.answer: Many things are mixed together, yet they still remain properly formed.

questions.question: What result would we expect if such creation were not under perfect control?
questions.answer: We would expect disorder, mistakes, or lack of distinction.

questions.question: Since those problems do not appear, what does the passage conclude?
questions.answer: It concludes that only a unique and all-powerful Being can be behind such creation.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about creating something enormous?
questions.answer: Something enormous is no harder for Allah than something tiny.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about creating many individuals at once?
questions.answer: Multiplicity does not burden Divine power.

questions.question: Which example shows that beginning small does not limit what can be produced?
questions.answer: The example of a tiny seed and a towering tree.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about seeing these deeds important for comprehension?
questions.answer: It reminds readers that the evidence is present in the created world around them.

questions.question: How should this passage shape a believer’s view of Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It should strengthen certainty that Allah’s power is absolute and beyond all limits.

questions.question: Which living things are highlighted first in this discussion?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the balance between ease and excellence?
questions.answer: It says creation is effortless for Allah while still showing amazing craftsmanship.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the relation between quantity and quality?
questions.answer: Even when things are very numerous, their quality and uniqueness remain.

questions.question: Why is the absence of deficiency important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that creation is not weak, partial, or accidental.

questions.question: What kind of Being does the passage say can create in this way?
questions.answer: A single unique Being with unlimited power.

questions.question: How does the passage challenge the human habit of thinking bigger things are harder to make?
questions.answer: It says the biggest and the smallest are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: What comparison answers the idea that creating a whole group must be harder than creating one individual?
questions.answer: The passage says a whole species is as easy as one of its members.

questions.question: What comparison answers the idea that world-sized actions must be harder than local ones?
questions.answer: It says reviving the whole earth is as easy as bringing a tree to life.

questions.question: What comparison answers the idea that a giant final form must be harder than a tiny starting point?
questions.answer: It says raising a huge tree is as easy as producing a seed.

questions.question: What does the repeated pattern of comparisons help the reader notice?
questions.answer: It helps the reader notice that no kind of scale creates difficulty for Divine power.

questions.question: If you had to give this passage a short theme, what would it be?
questions.answer: Allah’s power creates all things with equal ease, no matter how great or small.
